owner: Canonical Powerhouse Security Operations / Supabase backend
root_cause: One active Edge Function accepted a hard-coded repair token embedded in source. Another compared the caller header with an empty default when a recovery secret was unset, potentially accepting missing credentials.
prevention_rule: Privileged diagnostics must authorize before connecting to Netlify or Postgres. Hard-coded repair tokens are forbidden. A missing or weak environment secret must NEVER match an empty header. Accept only service-owned credentials or an explicitly configured strong legacy recovery token, verify with constant-time digest comparison, and suppress raw backend exceptions.

evidence.known_caller_evidence: 0 pg_cron references for either slug; no confirmed external caller attribution

proof_boundary: Live source is deployed and verified. Do not claim external 401/405 response tested or a safe authorized call completed; old consumers using hard-coded x-repair-token may need credential migration.
customer_outcome: Make two sensitive repair/inspection endpoints fail closed while keeping production website and hockey PWA unchanged.
